Stone & Ore Gallery

Gold Doré

Unrefined gold–silver alloy cast at the mine, stamped and weighed; the raw heartbeat of the precious-metals trade.

CompositionGold–silver alloy (85–95% Au, ±Cu)
Chemical formulaAu (native element)
Hardness (Mohs)2.5–3
Specific gravity~16–18
Texture / colorCast metallic yellow bars
FormationGravity/cyanide recovery from lode or placer deposits, melted at the mine
Found inEthiopia (Asosa, Adola), Ghana, South Africa, China
Common usesBullion refining, investment reserves, electronics

Emerald Rough

Green beryl in its natural host matrix — treasured for millennia; the May birthstone and one of the 'big four' gems.

CompositionBeryl colored by Cr/V
Chemical formulaBe₃Al₂Si₆O₁₈
Hardness (Mohs)7.5–8
Specific gravity2.70–2.78
Texture / colorGreen hexagonal prisms in host matrix
FormationHydrothermal/metasomatic fluids in pegmatite & mafic host rocks
Found inEthiopia (Weg Tena, Shakiso), Colombia, Zambia, Brazil
Common usesFine jewelry, collector crystals

Pyrite

Brassy cubic crystals — 'fool's gold'. Sulfuric-acid feedstock and a favorite of mineral collectors.

CompositionIron sulfide
Chemical formulaFeS₂
Hardness (Mohs)6–6.5
Specific gravity4.9–5.2
Texture / colorBrassy cubic crystals, pale green-black streak
FormationHydrothermal veins, sedimentary beds, metamorphic rocks
Found inPeru, Spain, China, Ethiopia
Common usesSulfuric-acid feedstock, collector specimens

Smoky Quartz

SiO₂ colored brown by natural irradiation. Transparent hexagonal prisms; a durable (Mohs 7) favorite for jewelry and carving.

CompositionQuartz colored by natural irradiation
Chemical formulaSiO₂
Hardness (Mohs)7
Specific gravity2.65
Texture / colorTransparent brown hexagonal prisms
FormationPegmatites & alpine fissures; irradiation of quartz
Found inBrazil, Switzerland, Madagascar, Ethiopia
Common usesJewelry, carving, collector specimens

Lepidolite

A lilac to rose-pink mica and one of the richest sources of lithium — the metal powering the world's batteries.

CompositionLithium-bearing mica
Chemical formulaK(Li,Al)₃(Si,Al)₄O₁₀(F,OH)₂
Hardness (Mohs)2.5–3
Specific gravity2.8–2.9
Texture / colorLilac-to-rose scaly aggregates, pearly sheen
FormationLate-stage, Li-enriched granitic pegmatites
Found inEthiopia, Zimbabwe (Bikita), Brazil, China
Common usesLithium carbonate feedstock (batteries), mica insulators

Kyanite Blades

Sky-blue bladed crystals with a curious split personality: hardness 4.5 along the length, 7 across it. A premium refractory raw material.

CompositionAluminosilicate (polymorph of andalusite/sillimanite)
Chemical formulaAl₂SiO₅
Hardness (Mohs)4.5 along / 7 across
Specific gravity3.53–3.65
Texture / colorSky-blue bladed crystals, glassy luster
FormationRegional (Barrovian) metamorphism of clay-rich sediments
Found inEthiopia, Kenya, India, USA, Brazil
Common usesHigh-alumina refractories, ceramics

Kyanite (weathered)

Blade fragments with rust-brown iron-oxide staining at the surface; the blue interior remains the same prized aluminosilicate.

CompositionAluminosilicate with surface iron-oxide staining
Chemical formulaAl₂SiO₅
Hardness (Mohs)4.5 along / 7 across
Specific gravity3.53–3.65
Texture / colorBlade fragments, rust-stained edges, blue interior
FormationMetamorphic; weathering oxidizes surface iron
Found inEthiopia, Kenya, India, USA
Common usesHigh-alumina refractories, ceramics

Kyanite (massive)

Massive blue-green kyanite in pegmatitic habit — the same Al₂SiO₅ refractory mineral in compact, iron-stained form.

CompositionAluminosilicate, massive habit
Chemical formulaAl₂SiO₅
Hardness (Mohs)4.5–7
Specific gravity3.53–3.65
Texture / colorMassive blue-green with iron staining
FormationRegional metamorphism; contact zones of pegmatites
Found inEthiopia, Kenya, India, USA, Brazil
Common usesRefractories, ceramic bodies

CompositionQuartz with fluid inclusions
Chemical formulaSiO₂
Hardness (Mohs)7

Frosted white lumps of silicon dioxide, Mohs hardness 7. Raw material for glass, foundry sands, and lapidary work worldwide.

CompositionMassive quartz
Chemical formulaSiO₂
Hardness (Mohs)7
Specific gravity2.65
Texture / colorFrosted white lumps with oxide staining

Milky Quartz on Matrix

White crystalline quartz with dark specks (graphite/mica inclusions) on a drusy matrix — a characterful cabinet specimen.

CompositionQuartz with dark mineral inclusions
Chemical formulaSiO₂
Hardness (Mohs)7

Graphite

Crystalline carbon: steel-gray to black, greasy feel, marks paper. Essential for batteries, electrodes, lubricants and — famously — pencils.

CompositionCrystalline carbon
Chemical formulaC
Hardness (Mohs)1–2
Specific gravity2.09–2.23
Texture / colorSteel-gray to black lumps, greasy
FormationMetamorphism of organic-rich sediments (or igneous)
Found inChina, India, Brazil, Mozambique
Common usesBattery anodes, electrodes, lubricants, pencils

Chromite

FeCr₂O₄, the only commercial chromium ore. Black-brown, submetallic luster, very dense; the backbone of stainless steel and ferrochrome.

CompositionIron chromium oxide
Chemical formulaFeCr₂O₄
Hardness (Mohs)5.5–6
Specific gravity4.5–4.8
Texture / colorMassive black, submetallic, very dense
FormationMagmatic segregation in ultramafic rocks
Found inSouth Africa, Turkey, Kazakhstan, Ethiopia
Common usesFerrochrome/stainless steel, refractories

Magnetite

Fe₃O₄, the most magnetic mineral on Earth. Black, submetallic, ~72% iron — the highest-grade iron ore known.

CompositionIron oxide; most magnetic natural mineral
Chemical formulaFe₃O₄
Hardness (Mohs)5.5–6.5
Specific gravity5.17–5.18
Texture / colorBlack, submetallic, strongly magnetic lumps
FormationMagmatic segregation, skarns, banded iron formations
Found inSweden, China, Brazil, Ethiopia
Common usesHighest-grade iron ore, steelmaking

Tourmaline Pegmatite

Feldspar–quartz matrix streaked with black schorl tourmaline — a classic combination from lithium-rich pegmatite fields.

CompositionFeldspar–quartz matrix with schorl tourmaline
Chemical formulaNaFe₃Al₆(BO₃)₃Si₆O₁₈(OH)₄ (schorl)
Hardness (Mohs)7–7.5
Specific gravity2.8–3.3
Texture / colorBlack tourmaline specks in pale feldspar
FormationBoron-rich late-stage pegmatite fluids
Found inEthiopia, Namibia, Brazil, Madagascar
Common usesColored-gem exploration, collector specimens

Feldspar Pegmatite

The coarsest rock on Earth, with interlocking crystals of quartz, feldspar and mica several centimeters across. Mother-rock of many gems.

CompositionQuartz + K-feldspar + mica
Chemical formulaKAlSi₃O₈ (feldspar), SiO₂ (quartz)
Hardness (Mohs)6–7
Specific gravity2.6–2.8
Texture / colorCoarse interlocking crystals, cm-scale
FormationResidual melts of granite crystallization
Found inWorldwide
Common usesCeramic/glass feldspar; mother-rock of gems

Lithium Pegmatite

An exceptionally coarse igneous rock where leftover magma grows meter-scale crystals of quartz, feldspar and lithium micas — a direct battery-metal feedstock.

CompositionQuartz + feldspar + lepidolite/spodumene
Chemical formulaComposite rock (Li micas/pyroxenes)
Hardness (Mohs)6–7 (gangue); 2.5–3.5 (Li minerals)
Specific gravity2.6–3.1
Texture / colorVery coarse-grained gray blocks
FormationExtreme fractionation of granitic magma
Found inEthiopia, Zimbabwe, Australia, China
Common usesLithium extraction (batteries), ceramic-grade feldspar

Muscovite Mica Schist

Silvery to rose-tinted mica sheets within a schistose matrix; muscovite is valued for insulation, paints and pearlescent finishes.

CompositionMuscovite mica + quartz in foliated matrix
Chemical formulaKAl₂(AlSi₃O₁₀)(OH)₂ (muscovite)
Hardness (Mohs)2–2.5 (mica); 7 (quartz)
Specific gravity2.76–2.88
Texture / colorLight gray, foliated layers
FormationLow–medium grade regional metamorphism
Found inIndia, Brazil, Ethiopia
Common usesElectrical insulation, pearlescent paints, decorative stone

Conglomerate

Sedimentary rock of rounded pebbles bound in a sandy matrix — natural 'pudding stone'. A characterful choice for feature walls and landscaping.

CompositionRounded quartzite/granite pebbles in sandy matrix
Chemical formulaClastic rock (SiO₂-dominated clasts)
Hardness (Mohs)6–7 (clast-dependent)
Specific gravity2.6–2.7
Texture / colorCemented rounded gravels — 'pudding stone'
FormationCemented river & lake gravels (diagenesis)
Found inWidespread; river terraces worldwide
Common usesConstruction aggregate, feature walls, landscaping
